title: Edge traffic oscillation mitigation and stream-resume protocol
creator: Mateo Ruiz
description:
Problem statement: During active-active multi-region operation we occasionally observe ‘traffic oscillation’ where short-lived spikes and reactive failover policies cause repeated traffic shifts for a subset of streaming sessions. That leads to partial session duplication, KV-cache thrash, higher token costs, and visible latency / partial-response incidents for streaming clients.

Goal: Design and implement an edge-side orchestration layer and a complementary stream-resume protocol that prevents oscillatory routing, preserves KV/cache continuity where possible, safely drains traffic under failure, and provides clear SLO-bound knobs (latency, availability, error-rate) for hosted API customers. The solution must work for both short-request and long-lived streaming sessions and integrate with existing circuit-breaker and load-shedding frameworks.

Scope:
- Traffic stabilization at edge gateways across two or more active regions.
- A lightweight session resume token and rehydration flow for streaming sessions that can be used on region handover.
- Circuit-breaker state enrichment so failover decisions are aware of streaming affinity and rehydration cost.
- Backpressure and load-shedding policies that prefer graceful degradation (e.g., switch to non-streaming fallback, reduce model size / sampling) over abrupt session kills when possible.
- Telemetry and SLOs: define metrics and dashboards needed to detect oscillation and validate protections.

Non-goals: full KV cross-region strong consistency, redesign of model routing layer, or changes to customer SDKs beyond accepting a resume token header.
decisions: Prefer asymmetric gradual-shift windows (60s default) rather than instant mirror switch to avoid ping-ponging
Introduce an edge resume token (signed, short-lived) with minimal state so downstream can rehydrate KV cache on sticky region handover
Circuit-breaker will add a 'stream-draining' state that delays failover for up to X seconds while attempting graceful rejoin
Load-shedding prefers soft downgrades (sampling, lower model, non-streaming fallback) before hard session termination when customer SLO allows
comments: 2026-02-26 - MR: Initial analysis of three incidents where clients experienced repeated region switches; attached packet captures and timeline in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RINF/Edge+Oscillation+Postmortem
2026-03-02 - PS: Implemented prototype resume-token generation and signature verification; pushed initial branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/2146
2026-03-04 - AV: Reviewed prototype; suggested adding a per-session rehydration budget and backoff to avoid thundering rehydration on mass failover
2026-03-06 - PM (Clara Ng): Confirmed product acceptance criteria; SLO targets for affected customers set to 99.9% availability with 250ms median token latency for non-failed streams

2026-03-09 - PS: Integration test shows reduced oscillation in synthetic traffic (from 18 oscillations/hr to 0.8/hr) using 60s dampening and 500ms resume-window; test artifacts: https://internal-ci.redwood.ai/builds/edge-failover-sim
2026-03-10 - MR: Security review requested for resume token signing key rotations; created ticket ENG-123789 to track HSM integration
next_steps: Finalize stream-resume token format and low-level header contract (PS)
